q: The longest railway tunnel in India is the:
e: The Pir Panjal (Banihal) Tunnel, about 11 km long on the Banihal-Qazigund section in Jammu and Kashmir, is the longest railway tunnel in India.

q: The world's highest railway arch bridge has been built across which river?
e: The Chenab Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir, standing about 359 metres above the Chenab river, is the world's highest railway arch bridge.

q: Which train covers the longest rail route in India, running between Dibrugarh and Kanyakumari?
e: The Vivek Express between Dibrugarh in Assam and Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu covers the longest rail route in India, over 4,000 km.

q: The headquarters of South Eastern Railway is located at:
e: South Eastern Railway has its headquarters at Garden Reach, Kolkata.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Civil Engineering (IRICEN) is located at:
e: IRICEN, the Indian Railways Institute of Civil Engineering, which trains civil engineering officers, is located at Pune.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Electrical Engineering (IRIEEN) is located at:
e: IRIEEN, the Indian Railways Institute of Electrical Engineering, is located at Nashik in Maharashtra.

q: Which is the world's oldest working steam locomotive, run by Indian Railways on heritage trips?
e: The Fairy Queen, built in 1855, is the world's oldest working steam locomotive and runs heritage trips from Delhi towards Alwar.

q: The 'Palace on Wheels' luxury tourist train is associated with tourism in:
e: The Palace on Wheels, launched in 1982, is the luxury tourist train showcasing the heritage and royal attractions of Rajasthan.

q: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway is unique in India because it uses:

options.B: Electric traction on the entire route
options.C: A rack and pinion system to climb steep gradients
options.D: The widest gauge in the country

e: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway climbs the steep gradient between Mettupalayam and Coonoor using a rack and pinion (Abt) system, unique among Indian railways.

q: The railway Golden Quadrilateral network connects:
e: The railway Golden Quadrilateral links the four metros - Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata - and carries a major share of rail traffic.

q: In railway accounts, the Operating Ratio indicates:

options.A: The expenditure incurred to earn Rs. 100 of revenue
options.B: The ratio of freight earnings to passenger earnings
options.C: The share of staff cost in total working expenses

e: The Operating Ratio shows the working expenses incurred to earn Rs. 100 of gross earnings; a lower ratio means better financial health.

q: The largest share of Indian Railways' revenue earnings comes from:
e: Freight traffic contributes the largest share, roughly two-thirds, of Indian Railways' total revenue earnings, far more than passenger fares.

q: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor connects Dadri (Uttar Pradesh) with:
e: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor runs about 1,500 km from Dadri in Uttar Pradesh to Jawaharlal Nehru Port near Mumbai.

q: In the Constitution of India, 'Railways' is a subject included in the:
e: "Railways" is Entry 22 of the Union List in the Seventh Schedule, so Parliament alone can legislate on it.

q: Which Mumbai railway station, formerly known as Victoria Terminus, is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
e: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Mumbai, formerly Victoria Terminus, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2004 for its Gothic architecture.

q: The Railway Board of India was constituted in the year:
e: The Railway Board, the apex body administering Indian Railways, was constituted in 1905 under the Indian Railway Board Act.

q: The first full-fledged railway workshop in India was established at:
e: The Jamalpur workshop in Bihar, established in 1862, was the first full-fledged railway workshop in India.

q: The world's longest railway platform is located at:
e: The platform at Shree Siddharoodha Swamiji station, Hubballi, over 1,500 metres long, is the world's longest railway platform.

q: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works primarily manufactures:
e: Chittaranjan Locomotive Works primarily manufactures electric locomotives, having switched fully from steam and diesel production.

q: The highest railway station in India is:
e: Ghum station, on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway at about 2,258 metres above sea level, is the highest railway station in India.

q: The 61st Amendment to the Constitution reduced the voting age from 21 years to:
e: The 61st Amendment of 1988 lowered the voting age for elections from 21 years to 18 years.

q: Free and compulsory education to children in the age group of 6 to 14 years was made a Fundamental Right by the:
e: The 86th Amendment of 2002 inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years a Fundamental Right.

q: Which Article of the Constitution empowers a citizen to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
e: Article 32 empowers a citizen to move the Supreme Court directly by writ for enforcement of Fundamental Rights; Dr. Ambedkar called it the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.

q: The first Chief Justice of India was:
e: Justice H. J. Kania was the first Chief Justice of India, taking office in 1950 when the Supreme Court was established.

q: The Battle of Buxar was fought in the year:
e: The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764, when the East India Company defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.

q: In the Second Battle of Tarain (1192), Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated by:
e: In the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192, Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan, opening the way for Muslim rule in northern India.

q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in the year:
e: The Non-Cooperation Movement, Gandhi's first nationwide mass movement against British rule, was launched in 1920 after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Khilafat issue.

q: The historic Dandi (Salt) March of Mahatma Gandhi began in the year:
e: The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930, when Gandhi walked from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to break the salt law.

q: The first Indian to become the Governor-General of independent India was:
e: C. Rajagopalachari succeeded Lord Mountbatten in 1948 to become the first Indian Governor-General of independent India.

q: A barometer is an instrument used to measure:
e: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure and is used in weather forecasting, since falling pressure often signals approaching bad weather.

q: A hygrometer is used to measure:
e: A hygrometer measures the relative humidity of air, i.e. the amount of water vapour present compared with saturation.

q: X-rays were discovered by:
e: X-rays were discovered in 1895 by the German physicist Wilhelm Roentgen, who named them "X" for the unknown.

q: Dynamite was invented by:
e: Dynamite was invented in 1867 by Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist whose fortune later funded the Nobel Prizes.

q: 'Laughing gas' is the common name of:
e: "Laughing gas" is nitrous oxide (N2O), so called because inhaling it produces a brief feeling of euphoria; it is also used as an anaesthetic.

q: The chemical name of Vitamin C is:
e: The chemical name of Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits and amla, is ascorbic acid; its deficiency causes scurvy.

q: The first Indian to win the Nobel Prize in Physics was:
e: C. V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for the Raman effect, becoming the first Indian to receive a Nobel in Physics.

q: The Ranji Trophy is the premier domestic championship in India for:
e: The Ranji Trophy, named after the cricketer Ranjitsinhji, is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship.

q: The Bhakra Dam is built across the river:
e: The Bhakra Dam is built across the Sutlej river in Himachal Pradesh, and its reservoir is called Govind Sagar.

q: The largest freshwater lake in India is:
e: Wular Lake in Jammu and Kashmir is India's largest freshwater lake; Chilika in Odisha is a brackish-water lagoon, not a freshwater lake.

q: 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' is the autobiography of:
e: "The Story of My Experiments with Truth" is Mahatma Gandhi's autobiography, originally written in Gujarati and covering his life up to 1921.

q: The Danapur division of Indian Railways is a part of which Railway zone?
e: Danapur division, serving the Patna region of Bihar, is one of the divisions of East Central Railway headquartered at Hajipur.

q: The Katihar division belongs to which Railway zone?
e: Katihar division, in north-eastern Bihar, belongs to Northeast Frontier Railway, which has its headquarters at Maligaon.

q: The Kharagpur division is administered by which Railway zone?
e: Kharagpur division, with one of the largest stations in the east, is administered by South Eastern Railway, Kolkata.

q: The Ratlam division belongs to which Railway zone?
e: Ratlam division of Madhya Pradesh belongs to Western Railway, headquartered at Mumbai.

q: The Palakkad division is a part of which Railway zone?
e: The Palakkad division in Kerala is a part of Southern Railway, whose headquarters is at Chennai.

q: The Kota division is administered by which Railway zone?
e: Kota division, in Rajasthan, is administered by West Central Railway headquartered at Jabalpur.

q: The Izzatnagar division, near Bareilly, belongs to which Railway zone?
e: Izzatnagar division, near Bareilly in Uttar Pradesh, belongs to North Eastern Railway headquartered at Gorakhpur.

q: In the locomotive class WAP-7, the letter 'P' indicates that the locomotive is meant for:
e: In the class WAP-7, W means broad gauge, A means AC electric traction and P indicates the locomotive is designed for passenger service.

q: In the locomotive class WAG-9, the letter 'G' stands for:
e: In the class WAG-9, the letter G stands for Goods, showing that this AC electric locomotive is built for freight (goods) haulage.

q: In the diesel locomotive class WDM-3A, the letter 'M' signifies:
e: In the class WDM-3A, W means broad gauge, D means diesel and M signifies mixed traffic, i.e. the locomotive can haul both passenger and goods trains.

q: The heritage steam locomotive shed of Indian Railways is located at:
e: The heritage steam locomotive shed at Rewari in Haryana preserves and maintains vintage steam locomotives of Indian Railways, including some of its oldest surviving steam engines.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Transport Management (IRITM) is located at:
e: IRITM, located at Lucknow, imparts training in transport management to officers of the traffic, transportation and commercial departments of Indian Railways.

q: The Indian Railways Institute of Financial Management (IRIFM) is located at:
e: IRIFM at Secunderabad is the training institute for officers of the Indian Railways Accounts Service and imparts training in financial management.

q: The Jagjivan Ram Railway Hospital at Mumbai Central is the headquarters hospital of:
e: The Jagjivan Ram Railway Hospital at Mumbai Central serves as the headquarters (zonal) hospital of Western Railway.

q: The Jagjivan Ram RPF Academy is located at:
e: The Jagjivan Ram RPF Academy, the premier training institution for officers of the Railway Protection Force, is located at Lucknow.

q: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in the year:
e: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1999, becoming the first of the mountain railways of India to be so recognised.

q: The Kalka-Shimla Railway received UNESCO World Heritage status in the year:
e: The Kalka-Shimla Railway was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2008, extending the Mountain Railways of India inscription that began with the Darjeeling line.

q: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway connects Mettupalayam with:
e: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway runs from Mettupalayam at the foothills to Udhagamandalam (Ooty) in the Nilgiri hills of Tamil Nadu.

q: The famous Batasia Loop is situated on which railway?
e: The Batasia Loop is a famous spiral loop on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway near Ghoom, laid out to negotiate the steep gradient of the hill line.

q: The Kangra Valley Railway runs from Pathankot to:
e: The Kangra Valley Railway runs from Pathankot in Punjab to Joginder Nagar in Himachal Pradesh, passing through the scenic Kangra valley.

q: The Bogibeel Bridge, India's longest rail-cum-road bridge, has been built across the river:
e: The Bogibeel Bridge, India's longest rail-cum-road bridge, spans the Brahmaputra river in Assam, connecting the Dibrugarh and Dhemaji sides.

q: The Chenab railway bridge rises to about how much above the river bed?
e: The Chenab Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir rises about 359 metres above the river bed, making it the world's highest railway arch bridge.

q: The Pir Panjal (Banihal) railway tunnel is about how long?
e: The Pir Panjal (Banihal) tunnel, about 11.2 km long, passes under the Pir Panjal range and is among the longest railway tunnels in India.

q: India's first cable-stayed railway bridge is the:
e: The Anji Khad Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir, built on the Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla line, is India's first cable-stayed railway bridge.

q: The Vembanad Rail Bridge, about 4.6 km long and among India's longest rail bridges, is located in:
e: The Vembanad Rail Bridge, about 4.6 km long, lies in Kerala, crossing the Vembanad lake waters near Kochi.

q: The Pamban Bridge connects the Indian mainland with:
e: The Pamban Bridge links the Indian mainland at Mandapam with Rameswaram town situated on Pamban Island in Tamil Nadu.

q: Howrah station, among the largest station complexes in India, has how many platforms?
e: Howrah station in Kolkata, one of the largest station complexes in India, has 23 platforms serving its suburban and long-distance trains.

q: The shortest-distance regular train service in India runs between:
e: The shortest-distance regular train service in India runs between Nagpur and Ajni, two stations only a few kilometres apart within the same city.

q: The first train in India to attain a speed of 160 km per hour was the:
e: The Gatimaan Express between Delhi and Agra, introduced in 2016, was the first train in India to attain a speed of 160 km per hour.

q: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor runs from Dankuni in West Bengal to:
e: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor runs from Ludhiana in Punjab to Dankuni in West Bengal, carrying freight traffic across northern and eastern India.

q: The approximate length of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, from Dadri to Jawaharlal Nehru Port, is:
e: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor from Dadri in Uttar Pradesh to Jawaharlal Nehru Port near Mumbai is about 1,506 km long.

q: The length of the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor is about:
e: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor, India's first bullet train project, is about 508 km long.

q: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project is based on the Shinkansen technology of:
e: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project is based on the Shinkansen technology of Japan and is being executed with Japanese technical and financial cooperation.

q: The 'Amrit Bharat Station Scheme' of Indian Railways relates to:

options.B: Redevelopment and modernisation of railway stations

e: The Amrit Bharat Station Scheme provides for redevelopment and modernisation of railway stations with upgraded passenger amenities and better integration with the surrounding city.

q: The 'One Station One Product' scheme of Indian Railways promotes:

options.A: One product of each district in the entire country
options.D: Sale of local and handicraft products at railway stations

e: The One Station One Product scheme allots outlets at railway stations for the sale of local, indigenous and handicraft products of the area, promoting local artisans.

q: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, launched in 2021, is primarily aimed at:

options.A: Coordinated planning and multi-modal connectivity for infrastructure

e: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, launched in 2021, is aimed at coordinated planning and multi-modal connectivity for infrastructure projects across transport sectors.

q: Indian Railways has set a target to become a 'Net Zero Carbon Emitter' by the year:
e: Indian Railways has set a target to become a net zero carbon emitter by 2030, mainly through electrification, renewable energy and energy-efficiency measures.

q: The standard traction system used on Indian Railways main lines is:
e: The standard traction system used on Indian Railways main lines is 25 kV AC overhead electrification, adopted as the uniform system for broad gauge routes.

q: The Mumbai suburban railway services originally ran on which traction system?
e: Mumbai suburban railway services originally ran on 1,500 volt DC traction, which has since been progressively converted to 25 kV AC.

q: The Maharajas' Express luxury tourist train is operated by:
e: The Maharajas' Express, one of the most luxurious tourist trains in the world, is operated by the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC).

q: The Deccan Odyssey luxury train showcases the tourism of:
e: The Deccan Odyssey luxury train showcases the tourism of Maharashtra, covering destinations such as Mumbai, Ajanta-Ellora and Goa.

q: The Golden Chariot luxury train is associated with the tourism of:
e: The Golden Chariot luxury train is associated with the tourism of Karnataka, covering destinations such as Bengaluru, Mysuru, Hampi and Goa.

q: The National Railway Week is celebrated every year in the month of:
e: National Railway Week is celebrated every year in April, around the anniversary of the first train run in India on 16 April 1853.

q: The highest award conferred on railway employees during Railway Week is the:
e: The Ati Vishisht Rail Seva Puraskar is the highest award conferred on railway employees during the National Railway Week celebrations, ranking above the Vishisht Rail Seva Puraskar.

q: RSPB, the body that promotes sports in Indian Railways, stands for:
e: RSPB stands for Railway Sports Promotion Board, the body that promotes, organises and manages sports activities and teams of Indian Railways.

q: The Fundamental Duties of citizens are enumerated in which Part of the Constitution of India?
e: The Fundamental Duties were added as Article 51A in Part IVA of the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

q: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
e: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in Part IV of the Constitution, spanning Articles 36 to 51.

q: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India relates to:

options.C: Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha

e: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution lists the languages recognised by it, which presently number 22.

q: The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution of India deals with:

options.C: Disqualification on the ground of defection

e: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment of 1985, contains provisions for disqualification of legislators on the ground of defection, popularly called the anti-defection law.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed under which Article of the Constitution?
e: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds office under Article 148 of the Constitution, which provides for this independent audit authority.

q: The Election Commission of India is established under which Article of the Constitution?
e: The Election Commission of India is established under Article 324, which vests in it the superintendence, direction and control of elections.

q: The Union Public Service Commission is provided for in which Article of the Constitution?
e: The Union Public Service Commission is provided for in Article 315 of the Constitution, contained in Part XIV relating to services.

q: The Attorney General of India is appointed under which Article of the Constitution?
e: The Attorney General of India, the highest law officer of the Union, is appointed by the President under Article 76 of the Constitution.

q: The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

q: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President at intervals of:
e: Under Article 280, the President constitutes a Finance Commission at the expiration of every fifth year, or earlier if considered necessary.

q: At present, how many Fundamental Duties are listed in the Constitution of India?
e: There are eleven Fundamental Duties at present; ten were inserted in 1976 and the eleventh was added by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002.

q: The Planning Commission of India was set up in the year:
e: The Planning Commission of India was set up in March 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India, with the Prime Minister as its chairman.

q: India's First Five-Year Plan was launched in the year:
e: India's First Five-Year Plan was launched in 1951, covering the period 1951-56, with its main emphasis on agriculture and irrigation.

q: The Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) was reorganised and led by:
e: Subhas Chandra Bose reorganised and led the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) from 1943 in Southeast Asia, giving it the slogans "Jai Hind" and "Delhi Chalo".

q: After the Chauri Chaura incident of 1922, Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the:
e: After the Chauri Chaura incident of February 1922, in which a mob set fire to a police station killing policemen, Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement.
